chunks: And from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Hamza al-Thimali, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said:

By Allah, Allah has not left His earth since He took Adam (peace be upon him), except that there is in it an Imam who is followed to reach Allah, and he is His proof upon His servants, and the earth will not remain without an Imam who is the proof of Allah upon His servants.
ai.seo_question: What is the continuous role of the Imam in Shia theology regarding divine guidance on earth?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir establishes the doctrine of *Istidrar al-Imam* (the continuous presence of an Imam), asserting that the earth is never devoid of a divine proof (*Hujjah*) from the time of Adam until the Day of Judgment. In Shia scholarship, this serves as a foundational argument for the necessity of Imamate in every era, ensuring that God's guidance remains accessible to humanity for interpretation and spiritual direction. The concept underscores the continuity of divine authority, linking the prophetic lineage directly to the Imams as the living evidence of God on earth.
